title: VPC Egress Controls for GPU Tenant Segmentation — IaC Adapter & Runbook
author: Evan Morales
content:
## Summary

This runbook describes the recommended architecture, Terraform adapter patterns, operational playbook and escalation path for enforcing VPC egress controls to achieve tenant-level isolation for GPU workloads. It covers: per-tenant egress NAT, egress filtering (HTTP/S and DNS), cross-account VPC endpoints for model artifact fetch, and an IaC adapter pattern that enables safe rollout across accounts and regions.

## Scope

- Applies to: Dedicated and Private GPU deployments (Redwood Dedicated and Private).
- Environments: staging, preprod, prod.
- Excluded: Hosted multi-tenant API frontends (handled by gateway-level policies).

## Goals and SLOs

- Enforce tenant egress policy with <=5s deployment time for policy changes (target).
- Prevent cross-tenant network egress with threshold: <=0.01% unauthorized outbound connection rate observed in network logs per month.
- Ensure fail-open is never used for enforcement; prefer fail-closed with clear rollback.

## Background and motivation

GPU nodes often run third-party model downloads, evaluation containers, and customer-managed init scripts. Left unchecked, this can: 

- Accidentally exfiltrate data to public endpoints,
- Consume unexpected egress bandwidth and increase cloud bills,
- Introduce latent dependency on external CDNs during inference.

Our approach: map each tenant to a VPC subnet + egress NAT/Egress Gateway profile and a managed set of allowed endpoints (S3 registries, internal model-store endpoints, telemetry endpoints). Use Terraform modules to generate the adapter resources, with automated policy reconciliation in CI.

## Architecture overview (textual diagram)

- Tenant VPC (account or subnet) --> Egress Gateway (ENI / NAT Gateway / Proxy EC2 ASG) --> Central Egress Filter (WAF, proxy ACLs) --> Internet / Partner Endpoints
- Model-store access goes over VPC Endpoint (privatelink) where available.

Diagram (text):

[Account A: Tenant-subnet-01] --(route to)--> [Egress-Gateway-A (proxy + ACL)] --(VPC peering/privatelink)--> [Central-Model-Store / Partner-API]

## IaC adapter pattern (Terraform)

We maintain a small adapter module (redwood_gpu_egress_adapter) that is instantiated per tenant account/region. The module coordinates:

- Egress gateway ASG (if NAT not available), with security groups locked to outbound 80/443 + allowed IPs.
- Route table entries forwarding 0.0.0.0/0 to the gateway.
- Firewall ACLs (managed ruleset JSON) mounted into the proxy instances via user-data.
- VPC Endpoint resources for model-store buckets and telemetry endpoints.

Recommended module inputs (table):

| variable | description | example |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| tenant_id | Logical tenant id | tenant-acme |
| allowed_endpoints | List of hostname/IP CIDRs allowed for outbound | ["s3.amazonaws.com", "models.redwood.local"] |
| use_privatelink | Boolean to prefer endpoints via privatelink | true |
| egress_mode | one of [nat, proxy, privatelink-only] | proxy |
| region | AWS region | us-west-2 |

Example module invocation (HCL):

```
module "egress_adapter_acme" {
  source = "git::ssh://git.internal.redwood/terraform-modules//redwood_gpu_egress_adapter"
  tenant_id = "tenant-acme"
  allowed_endpoints = ["models.redwood.local", "metrics.redwood-internal.local:443"]
  use_privatelink = true
  egress_mode = "proxy"
  region = "us-west-2"
}
```

User-data snippet applied to proxy instances (example):

```
#!/bin/bash
# install squid + custom ACLs
apt-get update && apt-get install -y squid
cat > /etc/squid/allowed_endpoints.conf <<EOF
acl allowed_sites dstdomain models.redwood.local
http_access allow allowed_sites
http_access deny all
EOF
systemctl restart squid
```

## CI/CD and safe rollout procedure

1. Create branch in infra repo and add module instantiation for target tenant.
2. Run `terraform plan` in staging account (automated via pipeline) and post plan PR.
3. Gate: require two approvers from infra-networking team.
4. Apply to staging; run integration smoke tests (see Test checklist).
5. Canary: apply to 10% of tenant subnets in prod region using `terraform workspace` per-subnet; monitor 30m.
6. Full rollout after 1 hour of green signals.

CI commands (internal runner):

- `make tf-plan TENANT=tenant-acme ENV=staging`
- `make tf-apply TENANT=tenant-acme ENV=staging`

## Test checklist (integration smoke tests)

- [ ] Model fetch via privatelink: curl https://models.redwood.local/health -> 200
- [ ] Telemetry endpoint reachable: curl https://metrics.redwood-internal.local:443 -> 200
- [ ] Blocked external host (example maliciousexample.com) must be refused by proxy (HTTP 403)
- [ ] DNS leak test from pod: `dig txt whoami.cloudflare.com` should resolve only via internal DNS
- [ ] Bandwidth sanity: egress bytes <= baseline + 15% (first hour after rollout)

## Metrics and observability

- Dashboards to monitor (ownership: infra-platform):
  - Egress Rejection Rate (per-tenant): alert if > 0.05% / 24h
  - Outbound Connections to Unknown IPs: alert if > 5 connections/min sustained
  - Model-store Latency (privatelink) 95th percentile: target < 200ms

Suggested logs: VPC flow logs (ingress & egress), proxy access logs, and CloudWatch metrics for ASG. Retain 90 days for prod egress audit.

## Operational runbook: common scenarios

1) Symptom: Tenants report model downloads failing after rollout
   - Check proxy ASG health: `aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-instances --auto-scaling-group-name <asg>`
   - Inspect proxy logs: `/var/log/squid/access.log` for 403 errors
   - Query VPC endpoint state: `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=tag:tenant,Values=<tenant>`
   - Remedy: If ACL overly restrictive, patch `allowed_endpoints` in module and reapply to CANARY subset, then roll forward.

2) Symptom: Unexpected egress spike in tenant A
   - Query flow logs to find top destination IPs: use the flowlog-search helper script: `scripts/flowlog-search --tenant tenant-acme --since 15m`
   - If traffic is to a legitimate but unconfigured host, add to `allowed_endpoints` with an expiration tag `ttl:7d` and open a security review.
   - If traffic is suspicious, escalate to Security (see Escalation).

3) Symptom: Proxy process crash on all nodes
   - Run `systemctl status squid` and collect `journalctl -u squid -n 500`
   - If crashes match a config change, rollback via Terraform to previous revision: `terraform workspace select prod && terraform apply -target=module.egress_adapter_acme -var-file=previous.tfvars`

## Escalation path

- Pager: infra-sre-oncall -> primary (15m), then infra-networking oncall (30m).
- If suspected data-exfil, open SEC-INC ticket and page security oncall immediately.
- Contacts:
  - Infra SRE oncall: #infra-oncall (PagerDuty)
  - Infra Networking owners: Priya Raman (priya@redwood.com), Lin Zhou (linz@redwood.com)
  - Security: security-oncall@redwood.com

## Ownership and run cadence

| Item | Owner | RTO | Notes |
|------|-------|-----:|-------|
| Egress Adapter module | infra-iac | 4h | Module PRs reviewed by infra-networking |
| Proxy ASG + templates | infra-networking | 2h | AMI and healthchecks managed here |
| Observability dashboards | infra-platform | 24h | Dashboards in Grafana under stack/egress |

Weekly maintenance: module tests run in Monday CI matrix; monthly security review of allowed_endpoints.

## Rollback checklist

- Run `terraform plan` to confirm revert plan.
- Target the CANARY workspaces first.
- Restore previous module input file `previous.tfvars` from infra-configs S3 artifact store.
- Monitor egress rejection metrics for 30 minutes after rollback.

## Security considerations

- All allowed_endpoints must be reviewed and annotated with justification and owner. Default rule: deny-all.
- Use KMS to encrypt any secrets (proxy credentials) and avoid plaintext user-data secrets.
- For third-party model registries, require signed attestations and pin TLS certificates where possible.

## FAQ

Q: Why use a proxy ASG instead of NAT gateways?
A: NAT gateways are convenient but lack fine-grained hostname filtering and can be more expensive at scale for auditability. Proxy ASGs allow transparent hostname/blocklist enforcement and richer logging.

Q: What if a tenant must access a broad external CDN?
A: Create a scoped exception with an expiry tag and review from security and cost owners. Consider peering/privatelink to the CDN partner where possible.

## Appendix: Quick troubleshooting commands

- list ASG instances: `aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-instances --auto-scaling-group-name <asg>`
- tail proxy logs (via bastion): `ssh ec2-user@bastion -- tail -f /var/log/squid/access.log`
- validate vpc endpoint: `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=tag:tenant,Values=tenant-acme`
- query flow logs: `scripts/flowlog-search --tenant tenant-acme --top 20 --since 60m`
